answer: I like to spend my weekends striking a balance between relaxation and being productive. In Bangladesh, the weekend is Friday and Saturday, so it has a slightly different rhythm from the West. After a demanding week, my priority is usually to properly [[unwind]] and recharge. I often start by catching up on sleep, which I sacrifice during the week. On Friday, I go to the mosque with my father for the midday prayer, and afterwards the whole family has a big lunch together, which is the highlight of my week. I then like to meet friends or family, perhaps for a meal or a simple outing, since spending time with loved ones is genuinely [[restorative]]. Once or twice a month, we take the bus to my grandparents' village home, where I sit with my grandfather and listen to his stories. I also try to fit in some of my hobbies, like reading or walking along the Jamuna, which I never have time for during the week. On Saturday evenings, I often meet a couple of old friends at a tea stall near the river. What I enjoy most is the freedom and lack of a rigid schedule; I can be [[spontaneous]] and do whatever I feel like. Honestly, I think weekends are essential for maintaining a healthy work-life balance. Without that break, the weeks would blur into one exhausting stretch. I make a conscious effort not to let work spill into them. A good weekend leaves me feeling refreshed and genuinely [[reinvigorated]], ready to face the week ahead with renewed energy and a clear [[sense of perspective]].

followUps.q: Do you ever work at the weekend?
followUps.answer: Occasionally, when application deadlines are close and students need urgent help. I don't mind now and then, but I try hard not to let it become a habit.

followUps.q: Were your weekends different when you were a child?
followUps.answer: Completely. As a child, I spent weekends playing cricket in the street from morning till evening. Now I value rest and conversation far more, which I suppose is a sign of growing up.
